## 3. Confounders & Limitations (from `docs/analysis_plan.md`)

- **No p-values or causal claims:** Spearman ρ is descriptive only; weekly series are strongly autocorrelated and 486 coefficients are reported across 9 scopes × 3 variables × 2 transforms × 9 lags.
- **Shared monsoon seasonality:** Both dengue incidence and rainfall/humidity/temperature follow strong annual monsoon cycles in Bangladesh.
- **Reporting & transcription artifacts:** Weekend/holiday reporting dips, hospital reporting backlogs, and unverified third-party transcription errors in Dataset A.
- **Outbreak dynamics:** Epidemic autocorrelation, exponential growth/decay phases, susceptible depletion, and vector-control interventions.
- **Spatial aggregation mismatch:** Division/national weather is an unweighted mean of district ERA5 grid points, whereas dengue hospitalizations are concentrated in dense urban centers (notably Dhaka; Dhaka division scope inferred from national totals matching DGHS published figures).
- **Edge truncation:** Dropping incomplete boundary ISO weeks trims partial boundary dates.
